title: test(parser): add a cargo-fuzz target for source parsing
problem: Parser robustness is covered by hand-written adversarial tests but not by coverage-guided fuzzing.
why: Fuzzing finds panics and pathological inputs that hand-written tests miss, directly protecting against DoS on untrusted source.
scope: Add a `fuzz/` crate with a target that calls `parse_source` on arbitrary bytes (lossy UTF-8).
Document how to run it locally; run it periodically in CI on a schedule.
guidance: Use `cargo-fuzz`; keep the target free of filesystem access.
tests: Smoke-run the fuzzer for a bounded number of iterations in CI
security: This directly targets the parser DoS surface.
deps: Adds a fuzz crate (not part of the main workspace build).
dod: Merged and green; scheduled fuzz job added.

title: test(core): property tests for fingerprint stability
problem: Fingerprint behavior is tested with examples, not properties.
why: Fingerprints are load-bearing for baselines; their stability contract deserves property testing.
scope: Property: line changes do not change a fingerprint.
Property: whitespace-only evidence changes do not change a fingerprint.
Property: rule id or file changes always change a fingerprint.
guidance: Use `proptest` with generated evidence strings and file paths.

title: test(report): golden snapshot tests for JSON and SARIF
problem: Machine formats are asserted piecewise, so unintended changes can slip through.
why: Snapshots make format changes explicit and reviewable.
scope: Store golden JSON and SARIF outputs for the corpus and compare on every run.
guidance: Normalize volatile fields (none expected; tool version is stable) before comparison.
acceptance: Snapshots committed with an update procedure documented

title: test(corpus): add at least three negative fixtures per rule
problem: Most rules have a single negative fixture, which is not enough to protect against false-positive regressions.
why: False positives cause users to disable rules; negatives are the defense.
scope: Expand `fixtures/corpus/<ID>/` with additional negative cases covering nearby legitimate patterns.
guidance: Document each negative's intent in a comment.
acceptance: Every rule has at least three negatives
security: Negatives must not weaken true-positive detection.

title: test(ci): run mutation testing on the core crate
why: Coverage alone can hide weak assertions; mutation testing measures assertion strength.
scope: Add a scheduled `cargo-mutants` job and track the score over time.
guidance: Start with the engine and fingerprint modules; expand gradually.

title: test(core): add a parser failure corpus
problem: Malformed-input coverage is limited to a few inline strings.
why: A shared, growing corpus of malformed Rust samples prevents regressions in error handling.
scope: Add `fixtures/parser-failures/*.rs` samples and a test asserting diagnostics and no panic.
guidance: Include truncated tokens, invalid UTF-8 boundaries, and mixed delimiters.
acceptance: Corpus directory exists and is exercised by a test

title: test(core): cross-platform path normalization tests
problem: Path handling has Windows-specific behavior that is only covered incidentally.
why: Windows contributors and CI should not regress path relativization or machine output separators.
scope: Add tests that exercise both separator styles and mixed-case drive letters in relative path logic.
guidance: Use `PathBuf::from` with explicit separators; assert forward-slash machine output.
acceptance: Tests pass on all CI OSes
